prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed the subjects of fluid mechanics and thermal engineering for a good understanding of the subject.

learning_outcomes.text: That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their area of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.
That students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work, lead and manage conflicts in a multidisciplinary group and/or a multilingual environment.
Ability to apply new technologies including information and communication technologies.
Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves and electromagnetism and their application to solving engineering problems.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and software applications in engineering.

syllabus_topics: Heating, air conditioning and ventilation installations. Calculations, modeling and design
Integration of solar energy in buildings. Calculations, modeling and design
Energy saving and efficiency in buildings. Systems and procedures
Topic 1: Thermal machines in the energy context.
Design and calculation of a heat exchanger.
Topic 3: Description of heating and air conditioning installations.
Basic processes in the Psychrometric Diagram.
Psychrometric analysis of some equipment and systems.
PART II : EQUIPMENT AND SYSTEMS FOR THERMAL INSTALLATIONS
Topic 8: Cold and heat distribution systems
Regulation and control systems in heating
Topic 10: Calculation of Air Conditioning loads
Thermal load due to infiltration / ventilation.
Cooling load due to internal gains.
Topic 11: Sizing of Air conditioning installations.
Calculation of air ducts. Fan selection.
Topic 12: Sizing of Water installations in Air Conditioning.
Calculation of piping networks. Pump selection.
Topic 14: Example of calculating an Air Conditioning installation.
Selection of regulation and control equipment.
Design of a Solar Thermal Installation.
Various case studies of thermal installation systems.
Air conditioning of a Restaurant with an AHU
Air heating and cooling installation for a car dealership
Heating of a detached house by water using a biomass boiler and radiators or underfloor heating.
Calculation, design and qualification of a specific installation
teaching_methods: Lectures based on multimedia presentations, theoretical expositions, calculation procedures, and practical exercises and questions.
Collective/individual tutorials for resolving doubts on theoretical and practical content.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and/or active participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities (attendance list and professor's notes)
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises (3 individual assignments, structure, correctness, originality and presentation analyzed)
Laboratory/field/ICT tools practices (Group work report, Public presentation)
